_doc: The list of 2026-11-14 (docs/improvements13.txt): the biomes' scenery. 926 scenery writes 'pieces' into brokenspire's WildPieces as n13_<name>#<n> and 'kinds' into WildSceneryKinds (FRDWildSceneryKind: a structure's fields plus place, uses, hazards, herd, ambush_r); 'fx' into WildSceneryFx as f13_<name>; 'channels' into WildChannelRules (the dry channels the world cuts, FRDWildWorld::MakeChannels); 'farsights' what is seen far off over a land (storm cells, a grass fire's smoke); 'mats' materials a part may lay its pieces in (mat=<name>); a kind's 'folk' its people (a townsfolk def, a title, its lines). The world places a kind in most cells of a 600 m grid of its biomes (FRDWildWorld::SceneryIn), a chunk lays it by the ruins' layout language (RD/RDWildRuin12.cpp: its parts; fx=<name> an effect at the layout's points, hours= day|night|dusk; inst=1 many as instances (patches); far=1 never culled (a landmark); L=mound|cone|ridge a rise of the land); RD/RDWildScenery13.cpp runs its uses (do=loot|forage|fish|honey|lore|heal|buff|fairy|milestone|rumour|climb|tracks), hazards (kind=collapse|sting|lurker) and herd (fauna:count;migrate;stampede;pen). A kind's front (its frame's +X) faces the road for place 'road', the meeting for 'crossroads', the water for a kind with need_water. Kit pieces (SM_N13_*) are blender_numpy/scenery13_kit.py's (926 kit).

uses: do=heal;x=2;y=0;r=3;verb=share;what=nomads' fire;reuse=600;text=They feed you mutton and tea and let you sleep by the fire.

kinds.name: hot_spots

kinds.title: Fungus glade
kinds.text: shelf fungi stepping up fallen logs, a ring of mushrooms: a forager's spot
uses: do=forage;x=6;y=0;r=3;verb=pick;what=mushrooms;things=Field Mushrooms|2|3|1,Herbs|1|1|0.5;reuse=600

kinds.name: hollow_giant
kinds.title: Hollow giant
kinds.text: an old-growth giant whose hollow trunk is big enough to shelter in
uses: do=heal;x=4;y=0;r=3;verb=shelter in;what=hollow trunk;reuse=300;text=Dry inside, and out of the wind. You sleep an hour.

kinds.name: mossy_walls
kinds.title: Mossy walls
kinds.text: mossy stone walls running through the woods from forgotten fields
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=4;r=3;verb=look along;what=walls;text=Field walls, deep in the forest. Nobody has ploughed here for a hundred years.

kinds.name: nut_cache
kinds.title: Nut cache
kinds.text: acorns and nuts heaped in the roots of an oak, squirrels and a forager arguing over them
folk: Townswoman|Forager|The squirrels were here first. The boars will come by dusk./Fill your pockets: the oaks gave twice this year.|4|2
uses: do=forage;x=2;y=0;r=3;verb=gather;what=nuts;things=Nuts and Seeds|2|4|1;reuse=600

kinds.name: charcoal_hearth
kinds.title: Charcoal hearth
kinds.text: a charcoal burner's smoking clamp, coppiced stools round it and his hut
folk: Townsman|Charcoal burner|Five days she burns, and I don't sleep for any of them./The smiths in Ashenreach buy all I make.|5|3
uses: do=trade;x=4;y=2;r=3;verb=trade with;what=charcoal burner;give=Bread|1;get=Wood Log|2;reuse=120

kinds.name: dawn_hollow
kinds.title: Misty hollow
kinds.text: a low hollow where the fog lies at dawn and dusk
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=stand in;what=hollow;text=The cold air pools here. At dawn the fog fills it to the brim.

kinds.name: harvest_shrine
kinds.title: Harvest shrine
kinds.text: a face carved in an old oak, gourds and candles at its foot: a festival ground
uses: do=offer;x=2.6;y=0;r=2.8;verb=leave an offering at;what=carved face;give=Bread|1;name=Blessing of the Harvest;dmg=0.05;armour=0.08;secs=900;text=The carved eyes seem kinder for it.

kinds.name: watching_aspens
kinds.title: Watching aspens
kinds.text: white trunks with black, eye-like scars that seem to follow you
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=look at;what=scarred trunks;text=Every scar is an eye, and every eye is on you. It is only bark. It is only bark.

kinds.name: clonal_grove
kinds.title: One grove
kinds.text: a whole hillside of aspens grown from one root: one living thing
uses: do=buff;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=rest a hand on;what=grove;name=The Grove's Calm;dmg=0.0;armour=0.1;speed=0.05;secs=600;text=Every trunk on the hill shares one root. It is very old, and very patient.

kinds.name: carved_aspens
kinds.title: Carved trunks
kinds.text: aspens carved with names, symbols and dates by shepherds and travellers
uses: do=rumour;x=0;y=2;r=3;verb=read;what=carvings;text=Names, dates, a heart, a crude map: one carving points the way to something.

kinds.name: gold_stand
kinds.title: Golden stand
kinds.text: aspens turned bright gold against dark conifers

kinds.name: beaver_stumps
kinds.title: Beaver-felled stumps
kinds.text: pointed stumps by the stream where beavers felled the aspens; elk have browsed the rest
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=look at;what=stumps;text=Gnawed to points, every one. And the low branches all bitten off at the height of an elk's mouth.

kinds.name: aspen_meadow
kinds.title: Aspen undergrowth
kinds.text: sunny, airy undergrowth of wildflowers and berries under the aspens
uses: do=forage;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=pick;what=berries;things=Wild Berries|2|4|1;reuse=600

kinds.name: aspen_edge
kinds.title: Grove's edge
kinds.text: where the aspens meet the pines: a cold camp, and someone watching from the trees

kinds.name: windthrow
kinds.title: Windthrow
kinds.text: a storm's swath of fallen trees, root plates torn up: a barrier, a bridge, a hiding place
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=-8;r=3;verb=look at;what=fallen trees;text=One storm laid them all the same way. You could cross the gully on that trunk.

kinds.name: hillfort
kinds.title: Hillfort
kinds.text: the earthen rings and ditches of an old fort on the summit
uses: do=lore;x=-4;y=3;r=3;verb=look over;what=ramparts;text=Two rings of bank and ditch, the gate on the side away from the wind. Older than any town.

kinds.name: chalk_figure
kinds.title: Chalk horse
kinds.text: a great horse cut into the hillside, white chalk showing through the turf: seen for miles
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=-24;r=3;verb=look at;what=chalk horse;text=Somebody scours it every seven years, or the turf would have it back.

kinds.name: terraced_fields
kinds.title: Terraced fields
kinds.text: terraced fields stepping down the slope, held by drystone walls along the contours
uses: do=forage;x=0;y=3;r=3;verb=gather;what=herbs in the terraces;things=Herbs|1|2|1;reuse=600

kinds.name: dew_pond
kinds.title: Dew pond
kinds.text: a round pond on the hilltop, lined with clay, that never seems to dry
uses: do=heal;x=7.5;y=0;r=3;verb=drink at;what=dew pond;reuse=300;text=Rain, mist and dew, held in the clay. It is cold and clean.

kinds.name: folly_tower
kinds.title: Folly tower
kinds.text: a lord's folly: a tower on the crest built for the view and nothing else
uses: do=climb;edge=1;r=3.5;verb=climb;what=folly;tz=10;reveal=2500;reuse=5;text=From the top of the folly the hills roll away on every side.

kinds.name: beacon_hill
kinds.title: Beacon hill
kinds.text: a beacon on the crest, ready to pass a warning from hill to hill; it burns at night
uses: do=lore;x=3;y=-3;r=3;verb=look at;what=beacon;text=Lit, it would be seen from the next hill, and that one's from the next. It is kept dry and ready.

kinds.name: quarry
kinds.title: Old quarry
kinds.text: a quarry cut into the hillside, its tools left lying, a cave behind its face

kinds.name: hillside_vines
kinds.title: Hillside vines
kinds.text: old vines in rows on a sunny slope, and a few sheep among them
uses: do=forage;x=0;y=6;r=3;verb=pick;what=grapes;things=Grapes|2|4|1;reuse=600

kinds.name: combe
kinds.title: Hidden combe
kinds.text: a hidden valley tucked between the hills, a hermit's hut in it
folk: Townsman|Hermit|You found the combe. Most walk past it on the ridge and never know./Take an apple. Tell no one./The hills keep their secrets in their folds.|5|-1
uses: do=forage;x=-6;y=6;r=3;verb=pick;what=apples;things=Wild Apples|2|3|1;reuse=600

kinds.name: peat_hags
kinds.title: Peat hags
kinds.text: black peat hags and sinking ground; lights drift over them at night
uses: do=lore;x=-12;y=4;r=3;verb=look at;what=peat hags;text=The lights drift over the bog at night. Follow them and the moor keeps you.

kinds.name: tor
kinds.title: Tor
kinds.text: a wind-sculpted granite stack on the hilltop: a lookout, and a lair
uses: do=climb;edge=1;r=3.5;verb=climb;what=tor;tz=5;reveal=2000;reuse=5;text=The granite is warm in the sun. The moor rolls away in every direction.

kinds.name: heather_gorse
kinds.title: Heather and gorse
kinds.text: heather blooming purple and gorse gold, dry enough to burn
uses: do=forage;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=gather;what=heather;things=Herbs|1|2|1;reuse=600;text=Heather tips, for a tea. Gorse flowers smell of coconut in the sun.

kinds.name: stone_row
kinds.title: Stone row
kinds.text: a row of standing stones, and the rings of old hut circles beside it
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=-4;r=3;verb=walk along;what=stone row;text=It runs straight at the hill on the skyline. Whoever raised it lived in those rings of stone.

kinds.name: peat_cutting
kinds.title: Peat cutting
kinds.text: peat banks cut into the moor, turves stacked to dry
uses: do=forage;x=0;y=8;r=3;verb=take;what=dried turves;things=Peat Turf|2|4|1;reuse=600;text=Dry enough to burn. The cutter won't miss a few.

kinds.name: moor_mist
kinds.title: Mist on the moor
kinds.text: a rolling mist that hides the landmarks: easy to get lost in
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=stand in;what=mist;text=Every way looks the same. The stone row was to the north. Or was it?

kinds.name: bothy
kinds.title: Shepherd's bothy
kinds.text: a lonely bothy, its door unlocked for whoever needs it, a ruined shieling beyond
uses: do=heal;x=5;y=0;r=3;verb=rest in;what=bothy;reuse=300;text=A dry floor, a fireplace, a note asking you to leave kindling for the next one.

kinds.name: grouse_butts
kinds.title: Grouse butts
kinds.text: a line of shooting butts across the moor, a hunting lodge and its gamekeeper
folk: Townsman|Gamekeeper|Keep to the path: the birds are sitting./The lord comes up for the season. Until then the moor is mine./You'll not have seen a fox? I've lost three hens to one.|-8|6
uses: do=trade;x=-8;y=4;r=3;verb=trade with;what=gamekeeper;give=Coarse Hide|1;get=Bread|2;reuse=120

kinds.name: moor_ford
kinds.title: Peat-water ford
kinds.text: stepping stones over a stream running brown with peat
uses: do=fish;x=1;y=-4;r=3;verb=fish;what=brown water;things=Fish|1|2|0.8;reuse=240;text=Trout, dark as the water.

kinds.name: switchback
kinds.title: Switchback trail
kinds.text: a trail cut into the slope in switchbacks, a mule train on it; stones come down from above
uses: do=lore;x=-12;y=6;r=3;verb=look up at;what=slope;text=Every switchback has its fallen stones. Nobody stops on this trail.

kinds.name: alpine_pasture
kinds.title: Alpine pasture
kinds.text: a summer pasture high in the mountains: cows, a cheese hut, a herder
folk: Townswoman|Herder|We bring them up when the snow goes and down before it comes./The cheese wants the whole summer. Taste last year's./You hear the bells before you see the cows.|5|2
uses: do=trade;x=4;y=1;r=3;verb=trade with;what=herder;give=Bread|1;get=Cheese|2;reuse=120

kinds.name: mountain_pass
kinds.title: Mountain pass
kinds.text: the pass between the peaks, held by a gate and its towers; a toll is asked
folk: Townsman|Toll keeper|The pass is the duke's, and the duke likes bread./Pay, and the guards on the far side know your face./Snow closes it by the first frost. Hurry, if you mean to cross.|5|-3
uses: do=offer;x=5;y=-1;r=3;verb=pay the toll at;what=gate;give=Bread|1;name=Safe Conduct;dmg=0.0;armour=0.1;speed=0.05;secs=900;text=The keeper stamps a tally and waves you through.

kinds.name: scree_slope
kinds.title: Scree slope
kinds.text: a slope of loose broken stone that slides underfoot
uses: do=lore;x=-4;y=15;r=3;verb=look at;what=scree;text=Every stone is waiting to go. So are you, if you cross it.

kinds.name: hanging_waterfall
kinds.title: Hanging waterfall
kinds.text: a waterfall dropping off a hanging valley's lip
uses: do=fish;x=2;y=-4;r=3;verb=fish;what=pool below the fall;things=Fish|1|2|0.85;reuse=240;text=The cold pool under the fall is full of trout.

kinds.name: mine_adit
kinds.title: Mine adit
kinds.text: a mine's adit bored into the rock: ore carts, rails, tailings

kinds.name: cliff_shrine
kinds.title: Cliff shrine
kinds.text: a shrine on a rock stack, reachable only by ladders
uses: do=climb;edge=1;r=4;verb=climb;what=ladders;tz=9;reveal=2500;reuse=5;text=Up the ladders to the shrine. The monks left long ago, the view did not.

kinds.name: rope_bridge
kinds.title: Rope bridge
kinds.text: a rope bridge slung across a gorge between two rock stacks
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=-8;r=3;verb=look at;what=bridge;text=Rope and planks and nothing under them. Someone mends it; the new planks are pale.

kinds.name: tarn
kinds.title: Tarn
kinds.text: a small dark lake cupped in a rock basin
uses: do=fish;x=1;y=0;r=3;verb=fish;what=dark water;things=Fish|1|2|0.8;reuse=240;text=The water is black and very cold.

kinds.name: goat_ledges
kinds.title: Goat ledges
kinds.text: mountain goats on impossible ledges, eagles over them
uses: do=lore;x=4;y=6;r=3;verb=watch;what=goats;text=They stand where nothing should. One looks down at you, chewing.

kinds.name: arete
kinds.title: Knife-edge ridge
kinds.text: a narrow ridge with sheer drops on both sides; its snow overhangs
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=-9;r=3;verb=look along;what=ridge;text=A path a boot wide along its crest. The snow on its edge overhangs nothing.

kinds.name: summit_cairn
kinds.title: Summit cairn
kinds.text: a summit cairn with prayer flags, and the bones of those who never came down
uses: do=offer;x=3;y=0;r=3;verb=leave a stone at;what=cairn;give=Bread|1;name=Blessing of the Summit;dmg=0.08;armour=0.08;secs=600;text=You add a stone to the cairn, as every climber does.

kinds.name: cornice_edge
kinds.title: Cornice
kinds.text: snow overhanging a drop, smooth and treacherous
uses: do=lore;x=-10;y=4;r=3;verb=look at;what=snow;text=It looks solid. It is not. The drop under it is a long one.

kinds.name: avalanche_chute
kinds.title: Avalanche chute
kinds.text: a chute cleared by past slides, broken trunks at its foot; more snow above
uses: do=lore;x=-14;y=6;r=3;verb=look up;what=chute;text=Nothing grows in the chute. Everything that did lies broken at its foot.

kinds.name: couloir
kinds.title: Couloir
kinds.text: a steep gully between rock walls: a way up, and a way stones come down
uses: do=lore;x=-10;y=0;r=3;verb=look up;what=gully;text=The quickest way up. The stones know it too.

kinds.name: rime_ledge
kinds.title: Rime ledge
kinds.text: wind-carved snow, rime-coated rock and ice-glazed ledges
uses: do=lore;x=-10;y=4;r=3;verb=look at;what=rime;text=The wind has built feathers of ice on every stone, all pointing the same way.

kinds.name: climbers_camp
kinds.title: Abandoned climbers' camp
kinds.text: frozen tents, ropes and a journal left on the mountain
uses: do=lore;x=-4;y=4;r=3;verb=read;what=journal;text=Day nine. The weather will not break. We go for the summit tomorrow either way.

kinds.name: cloud_sea
kinds.title: Above the clouds
kinds.text: a high rock above a sea of cloud, other peaks rising like islands
uses: do=climb;edge=1;r=3.5;verb=climb;what=rock;tz=3;reveal=3000;reuse=5;text=Cloud below you to every horizon, and the peaks standing out of it like islands.

kinds.name: dragon_aerie
kinds.title: Aerie
kinds.text: a nest of whole trees on a high ledge, bones round it: something enormous nests here
hazards: kind=wakes;x=0;y=0;r=7;who=Daemon;named=The Aerie's Drake;n=1;msg=A shadow falls over the nest: its keeper is home

kinds.name: crevasse_field
kinds.title: Crevasse field
kinds.text: ice split by crevasses, some open, some hidden under snow bridges
uses: do=lore;x=-12;y=-6;r=3;verb=look at;what=crevasses;text=The open ones are easy. It is the smooth snow between them you should fear.

kinds.name: serac_field
kinds.title: Seracs
kinds.text: towers of glacier ice that could topple at any time
uses: do=lore;x=-14;y=4;r=3;verb=look up at;what=seracs;text=They lean a little further every day. One of them goes today.

kinds.name: ice_cave
kinds.title: Ice cave
kinds.text: an ice cave's mouth, blue light within, meltwater running out of it
uses: do=lore;x=4;y=0;r=3;verb=look into;what=ice cave;text=Blue light, the sound of running water, and the cold breathing out of it.

kinds.name: moulin
kinds.title: Moulin
kinds.text: a vertical shaft where the meltwater drains into the glacier
uses: do=lore;x=-5;y=0;r=3;verb=look down;what=shaft;text=The meltwater pours down into the dark, a long way down, still falling.

kinds.name: moraine
kinds.title: Moraine
kinds.text: a ridge of rock and gravel pushed up by the ice
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=-10;r=3;verb=look at;what=moraine;text=The ice pushed all this here, and went back the way it came.

kinds.name: meltwater_lake
kinds.title: Meltwater lake
kinds.text: a lake of milky meltwater at the ice's foot
uses: do=lore;x=-11;y=0;r=3;verb=look at;what=meltwater;text=Milky with stone ground fine by the ice. Little lives in it, and it is cold enough to stop a heart.

kinds.name: frozen_thing
kinds.title: Frozen in the ice
kinds.text: something enormous frozen in a block of clear ice
uses: do=lore;x=-4;y=0;r=3;verb=look into;what=ice;text=Ribs as long as you are tall, held in the ice. Whatever it was, it is not a bear.

kinds.name: nunatak
kinds.title: Nunatak
kinds.text: a rocky peak poking through the ice sheet like an island
uses: do=climb;edge=1;r=3.5;verb=climb;what=rock;tz=4;reveal=2500;reuse=5;text=Rock under your hands for the first time in days. The ice runs away on every side.

kinds.name: ice_ruins
kinds.title: Ruins in the ice
kinds.text: the walls of something old, coming out of the ice as the glacier goes back
uses: do=lore;x=-9;y=4;r=3;verb=look at;what=walls;text=Cut stone, older than the ice that buried it. More of it shows every summer.

kinds.name: banded_wall
kinds.title: Banded cliff
kinds.text: a canyon wall in coloured bands, layer on layer, bones of something old in one of them
uses: do=lore;x=2;y=5;r=3;verb=look at;what=strata;text=Red, cream, red, brown: each band an age of the world. In the third from the floor, bones as long as your arm.

kinds.name: slot_canyon
kinds.title: Slot canyon
kinds.text: a slot canyon a few strides wide, light falling into it in shafts; the floor is no place to be in a storm
uses: do=lore;x=-14;y=0;r=3;verb=look up;what=walls;text=The sky is a crooked ribbon far above. Driftwood is jammed in the walls higher than your head.

kinds.name: canyon_creek
kinds.title: Canyon creek
kinds.text: a creek running down the canyon floor, cottonwoods along it, a sandbar
uses: do=fish;x=-10;y=0;r=3;verb=fish;what=creek;things=Fish|1|2|0.8;reuse=240;text=Small quick fish in the shade of the cottonwoods.

kinds.name: cliff_dwelling
kinds.title: Cliff dwellings
kinds.text: rooms of mud brick tucked into an alcove under the canyon wall, empty for an age
uses: do=loot;x=2;y=0;r=3;verb=search;what=rooms;things=Bread|1|1|0.5,Small Healing Potion|1|1|0.5,Straw Rope|1|2|0.7;reuse=900;text=Corn cobs in a bin, a cracked pot, a child's handprint in the plaster.

kinds.name: petroglyph_panel
kinds.title: Petroglyph panel
kinds.text: handprints, spirals and figures pecked into the wall; nobody can say what they mean
uses: do=lore;x=1;y=0;r=3;verb=look at;what=carvings;text=Handprints, spirals, a horned figure with too many fingers. Somebody wanted this remembered.

kinds.name: natural_arch
kinds.title: Natural arch
kinds.text: a span of banded stone carved by wind and water, the sky through it
uses: do=lore;x=-10;y=0;r=3;verb=look up at;what=arch;text=Wind and water and a long, long time. One day it falls; not today, you hope.

kinds.name: hanging_garden
kinds.title: Hanging garden
kinds.text: ferns and flowers growing where a seep leaks out of the rock
uses: do=forage;x=2;y=4;r=3;verb=gather from;what=seep;things=Wild Berries|1|2|0.8;reuse=300;text=Water beads on the rock and drips; maidenhair and monkeyflowers live on it.

kinds.name: echo_point
kinds.title: Echo point
kinds.text: a ledge over the canyon where a voice comes back, and sometimes something else does
uses: do=echo;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=call out over;what=canyon;text=You shout into the canyon.;echo=Your voice comes back from the far wall, and then a second voice, a beat late, that is not yours.

kinds.name: rockfall_scar
kinds.title: Rockfall
kinds.text: a fresh scar on the wall, toppled boulders under it; more is waiting to come down
uses: do=lore;x=-8;y=6;r=3;verb=look at;what=scar;text=The stone under the scar is pale, unweathered: this came down this year.

kinds.name: toehold_trail
kinds.title: Toe-hold trail
kinds.text: steps cut into the rock up a wall, an old rope ladder for the worst of it
uses: do=climb;edge=1;r=4;verb=climb;what=steps;tx=8;tz=9;reveal=2500;reuse=5;text=Toe-holds worn smooth by a thousand years of feet, then the rope. The rim, and the whole canyon under you.

kinds.name: box_canyon
kinds.title: Box canyon
kinds.text: a dead end of sheer walls: one way in, the same way out
uses: do=lore;x=-14;y=0;r=3;verb=look into;what=dead end;text=Walls on three sides and old bones on the floor. A good place to be trapped. Somebody knew it.

kinds.name: junction_cairn
kinds.title: Canyon junction
kinds.text: where side canyons split: a cairn, a carving and a warning scratched under it
uses: do=lore;x=-6;y=5;r=3;verb=read;what=warning;text=Scratched under the carving: LEFT TO WATER. RIGHT TO DEATH. And under that, in another hand: both wrong.

kinds.name: hidden_side_canyon
kinds.title: Hidden side canyon
kinds.text: a squeeze between two walls a body wide, and something kept beyond it
uses: do=lore;x=-12;y=6;r=3;verb=look at;what=squeeze;text=Sideways, breath out, stone on both shoulders. Footprints go in. None come out.

kinds.name: pour_off
kinds.title: Pour-off
kinds.text: a dry waterfall: a smooth lip of rock the flood pours over, too high to walk
uses: do=climb;edge=1;r=4;verb=climb;what=pour-off;tx=8;tz=6;reveal=1500;reuse=5;text=Polished stone, a scoop worn by falling water, handholds where it broke. Up and over.

kinds.name: tinaja
kinds.title: Tinaja
kinds.text: rock basins full of rain water: the only drink for miles
uses: do=heal;x=-3;y=-3;r=3;verb=drink from;what=tinaja;reuse=300;text=Rain water, warm, full of wriggling things. You drink it all the same.

kinds.name: outlaw_hideout
kinds.title: Outlaw hideout
kinds.text: a camp tucked against the wall: a fire, bedrolls and a lookout on the rim
uses: do=lore;x=-6;y=6;r=3;verb=look at;what=camp;text=Still warm ashes. Whoever they are, they watch the canyon floor from up there.

kinds.name: gold_wash
kinds.title: Panning wash
kinds.text: an old placer working on a wash: a sluice box, tailings, a mine's frame in the bank
uses: do=forage;x=-2;y=-5;r=3;verb=pan;what=gravel;things=Copper Ingot|1|1|0.6,Iron Ingot|1|1|0.4;reuse=600;text=Black sand, a few flakes of colour. Not a fortune; a day's wage, maybe.

kinds.name: flood_debris
kinds.title: Flood debris
kinds.text: logs and branches jammed high in the walls: how high the water gets
uses: do=lore;x=-12;y=0;r=3;verb=look at;what=debris;text=A whole tree, wedged across the canyon twice your height up. The water put it there.

kinds.name: hoodoo_forest
kinds.title: Hoodoos
kinds.text: a stone forest of hoodoos and fins, each with its cap balanced on top
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=0;r=3;verb=look up at;what=hoodoos;text=Spires of soft stone under hard caps. Where a cap has fallen the spire is already half gone.

kinds.name: dry_wash
kinds.title: Dry wash
kinds.text: a dry wash under a darkening sky; thunder far up the canyons
uses: do=lore;x=-13;y=0;r=3;verb=look at;what=wash;text=Mud cracked in plates, a tide line on the walls. When it rains up there, it floods down here.

kinds.name: banded_butte
kinds.title: Banded butte
kinds.text: a lone butte of banded stone, sheer-sided, a talus apron round its foot
uses: do=lore;x=-21;y=4;r=3;verb=look up at;what=butte;text=Layer on layer on layer, and on top a flat world nobody has walked.

kinds.name: mesa_pueblo
kinds.title: Mesa-top pueblo
kinds.text: a pueblo of mud-brick rooms on the mesa's top, reached by one carved stair
folk: Townswoman|Pueblo elder|One stair, cut by our grandmothers' grandmothers. Nobody climbs it we do not see./Up here the floods cannot reach us, nor the bandits./Bring us bread from the lowlands and you are welcome.|-6|-4

kinds.name: spire
kinds.title: Spire
kinds.text: a needle of stone standing alone, its top a nest of something
uses: do=lore;x=-11;y=0;r=3;verb=look up at;what=spire;text=A finger of stone, the softer layers wearing out from under the hard. Birds circle its top.

kinds.name: talus_apron
kinds.title: Talus apron
kinds.text: a steep apron of rubble round a mesa's foot; it shifts underfoot
uses: do=lore;x=-8;y=5;r=3;verb=look at;what=talus;text=All of this was the mesa once. A little more of it comes down with every frost.

kinds.name: overlook
kinds.title: Overlook
kinds.text: the edge of the mesa: the desert below to the horizon
uses: do=climb;edge=1;r=3.5;verb=climb;what=rock;tx=-4;tz=3;reveal=4000;reuse=5;text=The land drops away, red and gold and blue with distance, farther than a day's ride.

kinds.name: sky_shrine
kinds.title: Sky shrine
kinds.text: a slab with a spiral pecked into it, two stones leaning before it: at sunrise a blade of light crosses the spiral
uses: do=buff;x=-4;y=0;r=3;verb=watch;what=spiral;hours=sunrise;early=The spiral lies in shadow. The sun's blade crosses it only at sunrise.;name=The Sun's Blade;dmg=0.12;armour=0.05;secs=900;reuse=60;text=The first sun slides between the stones and a blade of light splits the spiral at its heart.

kinds.name: caprock_pools
kinds.title: Caprock pools
kinds.text: rain pools on the wind-scoured caprock, lizards sunning round them
uses: do=heal;x=-3;y=3;r=3;verb=drink from;what=pool;reuse=300;text=Yesterday's rain, warm from the stone. Lizards flick away from your shadow.

kinds.name: condor_ledge
kinds.title: Condor ledge
kinds.text: a great nest on a ledge under the rim, condors riding the air below
uses: do=forage;x=2;y=4;r=3;verb=reach into;what=nest;things=Bird's Eggs|1|2|0.8;reuse=600;text=Eggs the size of your fist. The parent's shadow passes over you, once, twice.

kinds.name: lone_juniper
kinds.title: Lone juniper
kinds.text: a single twisted juniper clinging to the rim
uses: do=lore;x=3;y=4;r=3;verb=look at;what=juniper;text=Half its trunk is dead silver wood. The other half still holds on, roots in a crack, older than any town.

kinds.name: storm_below
kinds.title: Storm below
kinds.text: the mesa's edge in a storm's season: weather passing below you, lightning under the rim
uses: do=lore;x=0;y=4;r=3;verb=look down at;what=weather;text=Rain falls in grey veils on the desert below; lightning stitches the plain, and you stand dry above it all.
